audit.title: Reporting Manager
audit.summary: This is a cleanly written conceptual page explaining Chainlink ACE's Reporting Manager — what it indexes, what the Reporting API exposes, and how the data pipeline flows. Its biggest strength is structural scannability: 11 well-scoped sections, sensible H2/H3 hierarchy, no oversized chunks, and consistent entity naming. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability and agent-runnability: zero JSON-LD, a missing canonical, no head-level dates, no comparison table, and — for a page describing an HTTP API with named parameters — zero example requests. The honest verdict: prose quality is Strong-band, but retrieval/trust signals and concrete API examples drag it into Developing.

recommendations.title: Add a runnable Reporting API example
recommendations.where: "What you can query" or a new "Example query" subsection
recommendations.issue: page describes filters and params but shows 0 fenced blocks
recommendations.change: add a tagged `bash` curl example hitting the Transactions endpoint with chain/time-range/policy filters, plus a trimmed JSON response showing a transaction record. Include the base URL and auth header placeholder.
recommendations.why: agents and engines lift complete, copy-pasteable requests; a described-but-unshown API is unusable to coding agents.

recommendations.title: Lead the page with a canonical definition
recommendations.where: directly under the H1, before "Why reporting matters"
recommendations.issue: *"This page explains what the Reporting Manager provides…"*
recommendations.change: open with a self-contained sentence: "The Reporting Manager is Chainlink ACE's managed indexer that records every onchain policy evaluation and exposes it as a queryable, read-only audit trail via the Reporting API."
recommendations.why: the first liftable sentence defends against parametric priors and gives engines a verbatim definition to quote.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased heading for the "managed contracts only" limit
recommendations.issue: the answer to "why isn't my contract in Reporting API results" is buried in a NOTE
recommendations.change: add an H3 like "Why don't my self-deployed contracts appear in the Reporting API?" restating that only ACE-Platform-deployed contracts are indexed.
recommendations.why: devs query by symptom; a question-phrased heading wins retrieval that a NOTE loses.

recommendations.title: Convert resource types + filters to a table
recommendations.issue: four resource types and their filter fields are prose+bullets
recommendations.change: add a table: Resource | Query by | Point-in-time (`as_of` / `from`-`to`) | Key fields returned.
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract structured reasons and build justified comparisons.

recommendations.title: Add concrete API specifics
recommendations.issue: 0 numerals with units; no latency, limits, or pagination
recommendations.change: state indexing latency (e.g. typical seconds to availability), any rate limits, default/max page size, and data-retention window if known.
recommendations.why: quantitative claims are among the highest-lift additions for citation.

recommendations.title: Add authoritative/external references
recommendations.change: link `PolicyRunComplete` to its event/ABI reference and link the Reporting API base to the OpenAPI/Interactive Reference at first use.
recommendations.why: inline links to primary sources raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Emit page-level metadata
recommendations.issue: JSON-LD absent, canonical MISSING, no head `dateModified`
recommendations.change: add `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `dateModified` mirroring the body "2026-03-31", a self-referential canonical, and `inLanguage`.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals improve agent parsing and E-E-A-T trust.

antiPatterns: Meta-opener instead of an answer ("This page explains…") at the top of the page.
Key limitation ("managed contracts only") reachable only via a NOTE, not a heading — a discoverability gap, not fluff.
No other anti-patterns: no keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references, no undifferentiated walls (median section 60 words).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is referenced from the page — good site-level signal; confirm this page is listed in it.
Head metadata could not be verified from the served HTML; pass raw `<head>` in the CLI for a definitive read on canonical/schema/dates.
Canonical URL and JSON-LD are typically templated site-wide — fix at the template level rather than per page.
